quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What must you do if you see this sign above your lane?

options.text: You can either continue through or exit from your current lane.
You can stay in your lane and continue through.
You must exit if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must exit if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means that lane will leave the highway. You can change lanes to continue through the interchange, or you must exit the highway if you stay in that lane.

questions.question: What happens when you slow down to look at accidents or unusual events?
questions.correctAnswerText: It causes traffic congestion.
questions.explanation: Avoid slowing down to look at accidents or other unusual events. This practice, called rubbernecking, causes traffic congestion.

questions.question: When making a right turn on a green light, what must you do?

options.text: Stop and check for police cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: You can turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says not to. When you turn, you must yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash.
You should increase your following distance as you drive faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, your chance of surviving a crash is very low. Faster speeds require longer stopping distances, so you need more space between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: What must you do at an intersection with a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Stop completely, check for traffic or pedestrians, then proceed.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Stop and stay stopped until the light turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check for traffic or pedestrians, then proceed.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, check for oncoming traffic or pedestrians, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: Why should you use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?

options.text: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
To warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: On rainy, snowy, or foggy days, it is hard for other drivers to see your vehicle. Headlights make your car easier to see. If you need to use your wipers, you must also turn on your low beam headlights.

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?

options.text: When the other driver signals you to return.
After you signal for three seconds.
When you see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before you return to your lane, make sure you are far enough ahead of the passed vehicle. Look in your rearview mirror. When you can see both of the vehicle's headlights, you have enough room to return safely.

questions.question: What must you do when you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights?

options.text: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
Drive to the right and stop.
Keep your speed and stay in your lane.
Speed up to pass the vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must change lanes to give it more space. If you cannot change lanes safely, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible.

questions.question: Should you use low beam headlights when driving in fog?
questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Always use your low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and can blind you.

questions.question: Which of these distractions increases your crash risk the most?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone, radio, or CD player while driving is dangerous and increases your crash risk. Even hands-free phones can distract you from driving.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, you should:

options.text: Speed up as fast as you can.
Wait for another driver to wave you forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. But first, you must let pedestrians and other traffic that are still in the intersection pass through safely.

questions.question: Lines that divide traffic moving in opposite directions are ____ colored.
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: You must use your headlights:

options.text: After 8 p.m. and before 7 a.m. during daylight savings time.

questions.correctAnswerText: From sunset to sunrise.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights one half hour after sunset. Keep them on until one half hour before sunrise. Also use them when it is hard to see.

questions.question: When driving near large trucks, you must account for:

options.text: The longer distance trucks need to stop.
The shorter distance trucks need to stop.
The quieter noise large trucks make.
The faster speed of large trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer distance trucks need to stop.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more time and space to stop. Stay where the truck driver can see you. Do not block their view of the road.

questions.question: A red traffic light means you must:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means stop before entering the intersection. Stop at the stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: You cannot park:

options.text: On a crosswalk or in a bicycle lane.
More than 12 inches from the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: Do not park on crosswalks or in marked bicycle lanes. When parking on the street, you must park within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.question: When you see angry drivers around you, you should:

options.text: Do not make rude hand gestures.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, stay away from them. Do not look at them or make gestures. Slow down, move over, or do whatever is safe to keep yourself out of danger.

questions.question: Looking far ahead while driving on the highway:

options.text: Helps you keep up with traffic.
Means you will not have to brake or turn suddenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Means you will not have to brake or turn suddenly.
questions.explanation: Look ahead at the road to avoid sudden braking or turning. This helps you drive safer, use less fuel, and keeps traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You must turn right or left.
A road enters from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a Y intersection ahead. You must go right or left.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: A traffic light is coming.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic light is ahead.

questions.question: If you park your vehicle in an unusual spot, what should you do?

options.text: Park with your reverse lights on.
Make sure other drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure other drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
questions.explanation: You are responsible for parking safely. Always park where drivers approaching from any direction can see your vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake hard to stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Apply the brakes gently and smoothly so your vehicle stops gradually.

questions.question: If you are driving slowly and traffic backs up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over to the right side and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right side and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is unsafe. If traffic backs up behind you on a two-lane road, you must pull over and let other vehicles pass.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes several times quickly.
Slow down gradually without braking hard.
Press the brake pedal as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without braking hard.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep straight. Take your foot off the gas and do not brake hard. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. Use gentle braking only if needed, then pull off the road safely.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines mean you may pass another vehicle from either direction.
questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no vehicle in either direction may cross them to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, leaving the curb, or merging is:

options.text: Not necessary if you use your mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: Always check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Do not rely on your mirror alone.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Last turn before a toll road.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flagger is ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs mean work zone activity. Be alert and ready for unexpected conditions. This sign tells you a flagger is coming whose directions you must follow.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is correct?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
They may use a loudspeaker to give directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Yield to emergency vehicles using sirens or horns with red or blue flashing lights. Follow their loudspeaker instructions. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only move when you are sure the way is clear.

questions.question: When you see a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is completely off the road.
Honk your horn as you pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is completely off the road.
questions.explanation: The law protects blind pedestrians. If someone with a white cane or guide dog enters the street, you must stop and yield to them.

questions.question: If you want to make a three-point turn and traffic is approaching, you should:

options.text: Flash your headlights and start the turn.
Let all approaching traffic pass before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let all approaching traffic pass before turning.
questions.explanation: When making a three-point turn, all approaching traffic has the right-of-way. Only turn when it is safe.
